title: Signature sendfile() Transfers
description: Transfers files to sockets with sendfile, avoiding userspace copies entirely. Data moves from page cache to the NIC via DMA; the application never touches the bytes. Static file servers live on it. title: Signature splice() Pipelines

title: Signature MSG_ZEROCOPY Sockets
description: Transmits with MSG_ZEROCOPY so the kernel DMaes from userspace buffers. Completion notifications tell the app when buffers are safe to reuse. title: Signature DMA-BUF Sharing
description: Shares DMA buffers between devices with DMA-BUF file descriptors. A camera buffer goes straight to the GPU or NIC without copies; exporters and importers coordinate via fences. title: Signature Page Flipping
description: Flips pages between the network stack and application instead of copying. The receiver's pages become the application's pages; only metadata moves. It is the oldest zero-copy trick, still effective. title: Signature PACKET_MMAP Rings

title: Signature RDMA Verbs
description: Transfers memory to memory with RDMA verbs, bypassing the remote CPU entirely. One-sided reads and writes move data at line rate with microsecond latency. HPC and NVMe-oF depend on it. title: Signature io_uring Networking
description: Drives sockets with io_uring submission and completion rings, batching syscalls to near zero. Registered buffers enable true zero-copy; one syscall submits hundreds of operations. title: Signature Buffer Pool Recycling
description: Recycles fixed-size buffers through pools so the fast path never allocates. Allocation is the hidden copy-cost; pools make it disappear. Sizing the pool is the tuning knob. title: Signature Header/Data Split
description: Splits headers from payloads so headers go to the CPU and payloads DMA to their destination. The NIC separates them on receive; software processes tiny headers while bulk data never moves. SmartNICs do this in hardware. title: Signature Checksum Offload
description: Offloads checksum computation to the NIC so the CPU never touches payload bytes. Touching bytes to checksum them is a hidden copy; offload removes it. Every modern NIC does it. title: Signature Hugepage Packet Buffers
description: Backs packet buffers with huge pages to cut TLB misses on the fast path. At millions of packets per second, TLB misses are measurable; huge pages remove them. DPDK made it standard. title: Signature NUMA-Pinned Buffers
description: Pins packet buffers and threads to the same NUMA node as the NIC. Cross-node DMA and access add latency; locality keeps the fast path fast. L3 forwarding benchmarks demand it.
